nodes.norm_label: price distance below ``peak`` that triggers the stop (atr-based if available).

nodes.label: Root conftest — runs before any test module is imported.  Critical ordering: bac
nodes.norm_label: root conftest — runs before any test module is imported.  critical ordering: bac

nodes.label: Backfill daily bars for the active watchlist over a long window.  One-shot opera
nodes.norm_label: backfill daily bars for the active watchlist over a long window.  one-shot opera

nodes.label: BrokerAdapter Seam (sacred rule)
nodes.rationale: Switching from paper to real trading must require only changing BROKER_ADAPTER env var, never code. qty is Decimal (not int) so fractional shares let a small budget take positions in high-priced symbols; the type is consistent across the whole seam.

nodes.label: Approved Architecture (db/api/scheduler via Docker Compose)
nodes.rationale: Services communicate exclusively through the database — no RPC, message queues or shared memory; SvelteKit is served as static files by FastAPI to avoid a separate Nginx container on the 4GB Pi.

nodes.label: Daily Job Sequence (7 scheduler jobs)
nodes.rationale: Ingestion jobs (06:xx) run in sequence writing to DB; analysis (07:30) reads only from DB, never calls external APIs; all jobs idempotent with misfire_grace_time=3600.

nodes.label: Multi-Portfolio Model
nodes.rationale: Performance is measured against net contributed capital (deposits - withdrawals) rather than a fixed starting figure; portfolio_id is a constructor argument to brokers, never part of place_order, keeping the seam intact.

nodes.label: Intraday Protective Sell (trailing stop job)
nodes.rationale: Interval job every 15 min during market hours sells on a trailing stop from per-position high_water_mark; stop distance ATR(14)*STOP_ATR_MULTIPLE tightened by a live-VIX regime.

nodes.label: Per-Portfolio Strategy Versions (A/B overlays)
nodes.rationale: A version is a named overlay YAML deep-merged onto config/strategy.yaml; versions are compared by portfolio-level NAV/P&L/alpha with no schema change to signal tables. One variable per experiment (e.g. v4 adds only momentum; regime multiplier deferred to v5).

nodes.label: Backtester (replays live pipeline)
nodes.rationale: Replays the LIVE pipeline (same engine, sizing, stop maths) over stored bars; strategy changes are calibrated here before going live — no new version ships without a backtest.

nodes.label: Market Entry Filter (benchmark vs long MA gate)
nodes.rationale: Universe-wide ABSOLUTE gate: BUYs downgraded to HOLD when the benchmark closes below its long MA, because rank-normalized versions always find a relative best and would otherwise enter on day 1 regardless of market trend. Fail-open: missing benchmark data never blocks.
nodes.norm_label: market entry filter (benchmark vs long ma gate)

nodes.label: v8 Regime-Switch Ensemble
nodes.rationale: Scores with the trend label (v1) config when benchmark >= 100d MA, else the chop label (v3); v8's own trading knobs are NOT switched because backtests showed most of v1's live loss was execution, not signal. Fail-open to the chop leg.

nodes.label: Microtrading Section (intraday same-session track)
nodes.rationale: Portfolio-scoped (portfolios.kind) rather than a parallel codebase; reuses the same engine on 5m frames. Validated by forward-test in paper, not backtest, because free intraday history (~60d) covers only one regime.

nodes.label: Default Watchlist Seed (runtime data, not hardcoded)
nodes.rationale: Symbols live as editable data in config/watchlist.seed.csv, loaded by init-db.sh only when the watchlist table is empty so removed symbols are never resurrected; keeps the no-hardcoded-symbols rule while letting the system trade out of the box.
nodes.norm_label: default watchlist seed (runtime data, not hardcoded)

nodes.label: Auto-Deploy on Merge (self-hosted Pi runner)
nodes.rationale: Every merge to main rebuilds the image (source + frontend are baked in) and rolls back to the previously deployed commit on health-check failure; a cron fallback covers runner outages and refuses to deploy over a dirty working tree so local work is never wiped.

nodes.label: CI Backend Job (ruff + pytest against TimescaleDB service)
nodes.norm_label: ci backend job (ruff + pytest against timescaledb service)

nodes.label: CI Frontend Build Job
nodes.rationale: No vitest on purpose — frontend unit tests intentionally skipped; the build is the gate.

nodes.label: Deploy Job (self-hosted Pi runner runs deploy.sh)
nodes.rationale: No actions/checkout on purpose: the live deploy dir with the bind-mounts the containers serve is the source of truth and deploy.sh fast-forwards it itself. Concurrency group deploy-pi queues deploys instead of cancelling in-flight ones.
nodes.norm_label: deploy job (self-hosted pi runner runs deploy.sh)

nodes.label: Consolidated Pinned Requirements (requirements.txt)
nodes.rationale: Pulls the four per-layer files via -r as source of truth; no requests/pydantic-settings/python-dotenv because code reads os.environ directly and uses httpx.

nodes.label: Dev/Test Tooling Requirements (pytest, respx, ruff, mypy)
nodes.rationale: Not shipped in the runtime image; installed into a throwaway container by scripts/test.sh and on ubuntu CI.
nodes.norm_label: dev/test tooling requirements (pytest, respx, ruff, mypy)

nodes.label: Compose Service: db (TimescaleDB)
nodes.rationale: TS_TUNE_MEMORY=512MB / 2 CPUs tuned conservatively for the Pi 4 RAM budget; host port kept inside the project's reserved 8030-8039 range so it never squats conventional 5432.

nodes.label: Compose Service: init (one-shot alembic migrator)
nodes.rationale: Dedicated one-shot service means migrations run exactly once per up, before api/scheduler start — no race between long-running services.

nodes.label: Dev Compose Overrides (bind mounts + hot reload)
nodes.rationale: Bind-mounts the repo so code edits need no image rebuild; uvicorn --reload for backend, Vite HMR for frontend; scheduler has no reload so it needs a container restart after job-code changes.
nodes.norm_label: dev compose overrides (bind mounts + hot reload)

nodes.label: Dev Compose Service: frontend (Vite dev server, HMR)
nodes.rationale: Vite owns the subdomain port (8030) and proxies /api to the api service so the public subdomain shows live edits; FastAPI moves to 8033 to avoid collision even when API_PORT is unset.
nodes.norm_label: dev compose service: frontend (vite dev server, hmr)

nodes.label: Docker Deployment Guide + DevOps Handoff
nodes.rationale: WORKDIR is /app (not /app/backend) because the code uses absolute backend.* imports and parents[2] path math resolves to /app; the launch prompt's layout would ImportError. Migrations run on the same +asyncpg URL; the only sync-driver consumer is the APScheduler job store.

nodes.label: Base strategy config (strategy.yaml)
nodes.rationale: Every weight, threshold and parameter lives here, not in code (CLAUDE.md). Any leaf overridable via STRATEGY__<SECTION>__<KEY> env vars; version overlays deep-merge onto it. Values are stubs to be calibrated by the Experiment Tracker.

nodes.label: Market entry filter (SPY 200d SMA gate)
nodes.rationale: Universe-wide absolute entry gate: block NEW buys when benchmark closes below its long MA; exits/holds never blocked. Governs first run / freshly reset portfolios so no version piles in at a bad moment. 200d chosen over 100d for out-of-sample robustness.

nodes.label: Base momentum indicator params (126/21, observation mode)
nodes.rationale: 12-1 style price momentum (synthesis 3.1): return over period bars ending skip bars ago, logistic-squashed. Base carries NO weight, so it is computed and persisted in observation mode only; v4 activates it (P11 phase 1).
nodes.norm_label: base momentum indicator params (126/21, observation mode)

nodes.label: Buy/exit hysteresis band (60/45 thresholds)
nodes.rationale: Gap between min_score_to_act (60) and min_score_to_exit (45) is a hysteresis band so scores hovering near the cutoff don't churn (synthesis 4.2).

nodes.label: Strategy version v1 (baseline control)
nodes.rationale: Intentionally a no-op overlay identical to the base, so v1 is an explicit selectable control arm in the A/B.

nodes.label: Strategy version v2 (loss-diagnosis fixes P1-P6)
nodes.rationale: Each key is the ONLY difference from base; rationale in docs/diagnostics/02-plan-mejora.md. Later found never to trade live: composite ~49 vs absolute gate 60 — kept as a cash-like baseline.

nodes.label: Strategy version v3 (v2 + rank normalization)
nodes.rationale: Built ON TOP of v2 so the A/B isolates the v3 effect. P10 (commissions) and P12 (freshness gate) are deliberately GLOBAL env knobs, not overlays, so every version pays the same churn tax.

nodes.label: Strategy version v4 (v3 + cross-sectional momentum)
nodes.rationale: v4 = v3 + one delta (momentum weight 0.40), per the one-variable-per-experiment discipline. Rationale: docs/diagnostics/04-plan-v4.md.

nodes.label: Strategy version v5 (v4 + macro regime multiplier)
nodes.rationale: v5 = v4 + P11 phase 2 delta only. Rationale: docs/diagnostics/05-plan-v5-v6.md.
nodes.norm_label: strategy version v5 (v4 + macro regime multiplier)

nodes.label: Strategy version v6 (v5 + fundamental weights)
nodes.rationale: v6 = v5 + activation of observation-mode fundamentals (quality 0.15, revenue_accel 0.10, earnings_accel 0.10). Missing values drop and remaining weights renormalize — never imputed (synthesis 3.3).

nodes.label: Strategy version v7 (v3 + wider trailing stops)
nodes.rationale: Live A/B and both backtest windows showed death-by-stops in chop (v3: 13 stops on 40 trades, win% 18.8). Candidate c4 from docs/diagnostics/07-plan-v7-v8.md calibration.
nodes.norm_label: strategy version v7 (v3 + wider trailing stops)

nodes.label: Strategy version v8 (regime-switch ensemble v1/v3)
nodes.rationale: The live A/B's core finding turned into a strategy: v1's momentum logic won the trending 2024-25 market, v3's mean-reversion wins the 2026 chop. Trading/stop knobs are NOT switched — v3's protective profile in every regime, because backtests showed most of v1's live loss was execution, not signal.

nodes.label: Strategy version v10 (regime ensemble + 21-session trend confirmation)
nodes.rationale: v9's post-mortem showed the MA100 test alone cannot tell an ADVANCING market from one drifting sideways above a still-rising average. Selected from a 4-candidate sweep by beating v7 in ALL THREE windows: chop +0.17%, long +44.81% (SPY +32.1%), and the never-used-for-calibration validation window oct-23 to aug-24 (+23.74%, Sharpe 1.94, maxDD -6.1%).
nodes.norm_label: strategy version v10 (regime ensemble + 21-session trend confirmation)

nodes.label: Micro version m1 (intraday control, RSI fade)
nodes.rationale: Micro reuses the base RSI/MA/ATR engine on 5-minute bars via the same score_universe path — no new scorer. m1 fades intraday extremes on liquid names (documented short-horizon tendency at 5m). Global costs are ON for every micro version so the A/B is fair.
nodes.norm_label: micro version m1 (intraday control, rsi fade)

nodes.label: Micro version m2 (RSI follow variant)
nodes.rationale: Identical to m1 EXCEPT the one variable under test: RSI passthrough (follow intraday strength) instead of mean-reversion (fade) — isolates the core fade-vs-follow day-trading question.

nodes.label: Micro version m3 (low-frequency micro)
nodes.rationale: m1 forward-test showed the 5m fade signal is ~zero-edge BEFORE costs while ~26 round trips/day at ~0.3% round-trip cost turned it into -8.5%/5wk. m3 keeps m1's signal but attacks the cost bleed: few, better entries (min_score_to_act 75) and no noise-flip exits.

nodes.label: P1: ATR removed from composite score
nodes.rationale: ATR was a near-constant volatility floor (corr 0.14 with the composite); weight set to 0 so it feeds only sizing/stops. Inherited by v3-v7 and all micro versions.
nodes.norm_label: p1: atr removed from composite score

nodes.label: P4: RSI mean-reversion mode (contrarian)
nodes.rationale: The biggest diagnostics lever: oversold scores high instead of buying overbought strength — the root cause of the -5.5/-6 pp alpha bleed.

nodes.label: P2/P3/P6: re-entry cooldown, stop floor, no pyramiding
nodes.rationale: P2: 3-day re-entry cooldown kills the protective-sell -> rebuy whipsaw. P3: 5% minimum stop distance so calm ETFs aren't stopped on 1-2% noise. P6: no pyramiding (AMD was 56% of the realized loss).
nodes.norm_label: p2/p3/p6: re-entry cooldown, stop floor, no pyramiding

nodes.label: P7: cross-sectional rank normalization
nodes.rationale: Each weighted sub-score replaced by its percentile rank across the day's universe before weighting, so the 60/45 buy/exit gate is RELATIVE to the universe rather than an absolute, biased threshold. Off in base/v1/v2 — the v3 delta.

nodes.label: P11 phase 1: momentum weight 0.40 activation
nodes.rationale: Cross-sectional price momentum enters the composite; with rank_normalize the sub-score is the symbol's momentum PERCENTILE across the day's universe — relative-strength momentum, the strongest documented single factor (synthesis 3.1).

nodes.label: P11 phase 2: macro regime multiplier (0.75/1.05)
nodes.rationale: Scales the composite by the day's macro regime score: risk-off (0) damps every score to 75% so fewer names clear the buy gate; full risk-on (100) nudges 5% up; linear in between; unknown regime = no effect.

nodes.label: v6: fundamental signal activation (quality/revenue_accel/earnings_accel)
nodes.rationale: Activates the fundamental signals computed since Phase 5 in observation mode; rank-normalized like everything else; a symbol without fundamentals is scored on its other signals, never imputed.

nodes.label: v7: wider trailing stops (ATRx3.5, 7% floor)
nodes.rationale: ATRx2.5 with 5% floor sat inside ordinary noise. Widening to ATRx3.5 / 7% floor halves stop-outs, doubles win%, ~30% fewer trades, and turns v3's 2-year bleed (-2.4%) into +5.1% while matching it in chop.

nodes.label: Regime-switch mechanism (SPY 100d MA leg selector)
nodes.rationale: Scores the universe with the trend label's config (v1) when the benchmark closes at/above its 100-day MA and with the chop label's (v3) otherwise. Sub-strategies are the existing overlays — no duplicated parameters, one variable (the switch) vs both parents. Lives inside DefaultAnalysisEngine, fail-open to the chop leg.

nodes.label: v10: 21-session advance confirmation for the trend leg
nodes.rationale: The trend leg (v1 signals + v1 execution, pyramiding allowed) engages only when SPY is above its 100d MA AND has advanced over the last 21 sessions (confirm_momentum_sessions: 21, confirm_min_return: 0.0); otherwise the defensive leg (v3 signals + brakes) runs. Stops never switch (stop_min_distance_pct constant in every regime).
nodes.norm_label: v10: 21-session advance confirmation for the trend leg

nodes.label: m3 anti-churn budget (max 5 trades/day, 60-min min hold)
nodes.rationale: At most 5 signal entries per session; a position must be at least 60 minutes old before a SIGNAL exit may close it — protective stops and the EOD flatten are exempt because risk never waits.
nodes.norm_label: m3 anti-churn budget (max 5 trades/day, 60-min min hold)

nodes.label: StrategyConfig (frozen pydantic, YAML + env override)
nodes.rationale: load_strategy_config(label=...) deep-merges a config/strategies/<label>.yaml overlay onto the base; TradingConfig fields are all-optional with None -> env/default fallback so the base config leaves execution byte-for-byte unchanged.

nodes.label: engine.score_universe (universe-level pass)
nodes.rationale: Runs one universe-level pass replacing each weighted sub-score with its percentile rank when scoring.rank_normalize is on; both run_analysis and execute_paper_trades call it, so there is a single universe pass and no divergence.

nodes.label: strategy_version = semver+config_hash
nodes.rationale: The hash makes an un-bumped config edit record as a distinct version (experiment-framework 2.1). Adding config fields changed the base config_hash, so A/B analysis must group by portfolio/strategy_label, not raw strategy_version.

nodes.label: PaperBroker
nodes.rationale: Fill model: same-day latest close x (1 +/- SLIPPAGE_PCT), instant FILLED; sells require sufficient held shares else REJECTED (no shorting). P10 commissions charged per fill, global env knobs.

nodes.label: PortfolioManager
nodes.rationale: Assembles AccountBalance purely from broker calls (get_account_balance + get_cash), never the DB cash ledger directly, so an in-memory MockRealBroker stays self-consistent. Takes an optional per-version config as a constructor arg — never part of place_order (seam intact).

nodes.label: Ledger-derived cash (never stored)
nodes.rationale: cash = sum(deposits) - sum(withdrawals) - sum(buys) + sum(sells) - sum(commissions) over the cash_movements and filled trade_orders ledgers. No mutable cash row; reconstructable after any restart. STARTING_CASH does not drive paper cash.

nodes.label: ingest_daily_bars orchestrator
nodes.rationale: Fetches, validates, upserts and commits; safe to re-run. ValidationReport.ok is returned but not enforced — bars are still written so analysis has something.

nodes.label: Single-hop provider fallback (yfinance -> Twelve Data)
nodes.rationale: Primary -> secondary once -> log + re-raise, by design: the job treats a raised ProviderError as today's fetch failed and relies on misfire_grace_time / next-day retry, not looping.

nodes.label: Observation-mode signals (macro_regime, revenue_accel, earnings_accel, quality, news_buzz)
nodes.rationale: Computed in run_analysis and persisted to signal_values but NOT passed to the composite scorer, so no trade changes until a deliberate activation (weights or a regime multiplier in strategy.yaml) gated by the Experiment Tracker. Ingestion jobs skip cleanly when their API key is absent — the pipeline degrades rather than fails.
nodes.norm_label: observation-mode signals (macro_regime, revenue_accel, earnings_accel, quality, news_buzz)

nodes.label: BrokerAdapter Protocol (sacred seam)
nodes.rationale: Async with qty: Decimal — the whole stack is async SQLAlchemy and the real-broker swap target is network-bound; Decimal supports fractional shares so a small budget can take a position in a high-priced symbol. get_cash() keeps PortfolioManager broker-authoritative so MockRealBroker reconciles with its own total.

nodes.label: MarketDataProvider Protocol (+ sub-protocols)
nodes.rationale: OHLCV backbone plus Fundamentals/Macro/News/Filings/Sentiment sub-protocols; all async and batch-oriented for the Pi. Swapping sources never touches analysis logic.

nodes.label: AnalysisEngine Protocol
nodes.rationale: CompositeScorer and SymbolRanker are separate injectable Protocols so the Experiment Tracker can swap scorer versions (synthesis 6).

nodes.label: backend.contracts DTO leaf module
nodes.rationale: Single leaf module imported by every layer to avoid import cycles; frozen Pydantic v2 DTOs deliberately distinct from session-bound ORM models, field names mirroring DB columns 1:1. Money/prices/scores are Decimal end-to-end (PerformanceMetrics is the one float exception, being numpy/pandas-based).

nodes.label: Trailing stop (protective_sell interval job)
nodes.rationale: The daily pipeline is blind between runs — a crashing position wasn't sold until the next day. Stop distance = ATR(14) x STOP_ATR_MULTIPLE (volatility-adaptive), else peak x TRAILING_STOP_PCT; the persisted 'atr' signal is a 0-100 sub-score, not price units, hence an on-the-fly recompute. Registered as an IntervalTrigger, not in JOB_SCHEDULE.

nodes.label: Per-position high_water_mark ratchet
nodes.rationale: Seeds from avg_cost and only ratchets up — a position that only ever falls still has a hard floor, while one that runs up trails its peak (take-profit). Initialized lazily; no backfill needed.

nodes.label: Live-VIX stop regime (tighten / panic-hold)
nodes.rationale: At/above VIX_TIGHTEN_ABOVE the stop distance is multiplied by STOP_TIGHTEN_FACTOR (exit sooner); at/above VIX_PANIC_ABOVE the job holds — extreme VIX is historically near the bottom, so don't sell the capitulation.

nodes.label: market_bars hypertable
nodes.rationale: The dominant table (66 tickers, ~16.6k rows/yr); the only compressed table (segmentby symbol, 180-day policy) — six months uncompressed for fast writes, older history compressed for multi-year backtests. Also reused for intermarket/regime ETFs — no separate table.

nodes.label: signal_values universal signal store
nodes.rationale: signal_id is a free string — new signals need no schema change; carries data_completeness per synthesis 3.3.

nodes.label: algorithm_signals hypertable
nodes.rationale: Output of run_analysis: score, action, reason, indicator_snapshot jsonb; made a hypertable so monthly_signal_accuracy (a continuous aggregate) can read it; realized_return/outcome filled by a later settle job.

nodes.label: trade_orders append-only order log
nodes.rationale: Migration 0009 added nullable commission (P10), backfilled NULL to 0 so historical portfolios' cash is unchanged.

nodes.label: watchlist table (runtime-populated universe)
nodes.rationale: Ships empty; seeded at runtime — never hardcoded in source (CLAUDE.md rule).

nodes.label: Idempotent upserts on natural keys
nodes.rationale: Jobs may rerun within misfire_grace_time=3600, so every writer uses INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE on natural keys: bars (symbol,ts), signals (symbol,ts,signal_id), macro (series_id,ts), filings (accession_no), insider (accession_no,txn_seq), fundamentals (symbol,period_end).

nodes.label: Point-in-time vintage columns (release_ts / as_of)
nodes.rationale: FRED series and fundamentals are restated; release_ts/as_of capture when a value was published so the Experiment Tracker can avoid look-ahead bias. Full ALFRED vintage history is a Phase-2 upgrade.

nodes.label: Continuous aggregates (weekly_performance, monthly_signal_accuracy)
nodes.rationale: Fixed 30-day bucket instead of calendar month: CAs over timestamptz hypertables need a fixed-width bucket; robust on the Pi and avoids timezone-dependent refresh edge cases. hit_rate aggregates the pre-computed outcome column so the CA stays a pure aggregate — no forward-looking join.

nodes.label: Daily 7-job sequence (06:00-08:15 UTC)
nodes.rationale: Ingestion jobs run strictly sequential, each committing before the next; a 45-minute gap before run_analysis absorbs ingestion overruns. Guiding rule: never trade on data fetched outside today's intended window — a long outage skips the day rather than acting late on stale prices.

nodes.label: Ingestion vs compute job classes
nodes.rationale: Ingestion jobs (06:xx) call external APIs and write to DB; compute jobs (07:30+) read ONLY from DB. This separation is the backbone of every failure-recovery decision: a dead external API can only break ingestion, never analysis or trade execution. Ingestion failures degrade, never abort; the only fatal path is an invalid strategy.yaml (refuse to trade on an unvalidated config).

nodes.label: Trade order state machine (PENDING -> terminal)
nodes.rationale: Every order must reach a terminal state within the day; a PENDING order at NAV time is a bug and is force-CANCELLED. Replaying execute_paper_trades must not move an already-terminal order.

nodes.label: Scheduler reboot / misfire recovery behavior
nodes.rationale: APScheduler + PostgreSQL job store evaluates missed runs against misfire_grace_time=3600; coalesce collapses multiple missed firings. Past-grace jobs skip with MISFIRE_SKIP — no catch-up trading on stale data.

nodes.label: Filtro de mercado + reseteo de carteras
nodes.author: Claude (autonomous session)
nodes.norm_label: filtro de mercado + reseteo de carteras

nodes.label: Two color languages rule (--pnl-* vs --status-*)
nodes.rationale: Money (gain/loss green/red) and system health/regime (teal/amber/magenta) must never share a palette so 'system OK' never visually reads as 'made money'; token namespacing (--pnl-* vs --status-*) enforces it.

nodes.label: Color is never the only cue
nodes.rationale: ~8% of men are red/green color-blind and the dashboard's story is red vs green; every gain/loss element pairs color with sign (+/-), arrow, or shape so meaning survives grayscale.
nodes.norm_label: color is never the only cue

nodes.label: tokens.css design token system
nodes.rationale: Single source of truth for all colors/type/spacing as CSS custom properties; components must never hardcode hex/px; system fonts only to fit the Pi budget.

nodes.label: Information hierarchy: trust before numbers (T0-T4)
nodes.rationale: Health (T0) ranks above performance (T1) deliberately: a red P&L in RISK_OFF can be correct behavior, but a broken pipeline makes every number a lie, so health is always visible and pre-empts the performance story.

nodes.label: /compare route (NAV overlay comparison)
nodes.rationale: Overlays every portfolio's NAV with a shared crosshair and %-rebased/absolute toggle so strategy versions with unequal budgets are comparable.

nodes.label: CR-1: scorer buys overbought/extended (selection)
nodes.rationale: RSI passthrough weight 0.50 (BUY at mean RSI 66.6), ma_trend rewarding extension, and ATR inside the score inverted contradicted the approved design (synthesis section 3.2/3.4); corr(composite,RSI)=0.963. Root cause of most negative alpha.

nodes.label: CR-2: trailing stop too tight for low volatility (execution)
nodes.rationale: ATR x2.5 on calm ETFs gave ~1.5-2.5% stop distances, liquidating SPY/VTI/QQQ on normal intraday noise; 74% of realized loss crystallized in one cascade day (2026-06-05).
nodes.norm_label: cr-2: trailing stop too tight for low volatility (execution)

nodes.label: CR-3: protective_sell/rebuy whipsaw, no cooldown (architecture)
nodes.rationale: protective_sell was the only real exit path (scorer-exit threshold 45 unreachable when RSI keeps scoring BUY), and the daily job rebought the same stopped name next day (AMD stop 06-05, rebuy 06-08 +0.15% dearer); no cooldown/blacklist existed.

nodes.label: P1: remove ATR from the composite score
nodes.rationale: The master design reserves ATR for sizing/stops, not attractiveness; ATR-in-score injected a quasi-constant +5pt floor and tilted selection toward the most volatile names. One-line YAML fix, scorer renormalizes automatically.
nodes.norm_label: p1: remove atr from the composite score

nodes.label: P4: RSI mean-reversion mode
nodes.rationale: Raw RSI passthrough at weight 0.50 made high RSI (overbought) score high, buying tops; design never used high RSI as a buy. mean_reversion mode inverts the bias, gated by forward-test because direction for this universe was unproven.

nodes.label: P2: post-stop re-entry cooldown
nodes.rationale: Breaks the protective_sell <-> execute_paper_trades rebuy loop; implemented as a candidate filter per portfolio (STOP_REENTRY_COOLDOWN_DAYS), never touching the BrokerAdapter seam.

nodes.label: P3: minimum stop-distance floor
nodes.rationale: STOP_MIN_DISTANCE_PCT decouples stop distance from a calm name's tiny ATR so normal ETF noise no longer triggers liquidation.

nodes.label: Strategy v2 (diagnosis fixes P1-P6)
nodes.rationale: Delivered as a per-portfolio strategy overlay (config/strategies/v2.yaml) so v1 (control) vs v2 run as a live parallel A/B; v2 later found to never trade (composite ~49 vs absolute gate 60) and kept only as a cash-like baseline.

nodes.label: One variable per experiment discipline
nodes.rationale: RSI/MA/ATR collinearity means simultaneous changes cannot be attributed; every version delta isolates exactly one change so the A/B verdict is interpretable. Became the project's standing rule for v3-v10 and m1-m3.

nodes.label: Strategy v3 (= v2 + P7 rank-normalization)
nodes.rationale: v3 builds on v2 so the A/B isolates the rank-normalization delta; live it became the only profitable daily version in the 2026 sideways window.

nodes.label: P7: cross-sectional rank-normalization (scoring.rank_normalize)
nodes.rationale: The 60/45 buy/exit gate was absolute and biased; replacing each weighted sub-score with its percentile across the day's universe makes the gate relative. Implemented one layer above the per-symbol scorer, in engine.score_universe, so run_analysis and execute_paper_trades share a single universe pass.

nodes.label: P10: commission model in PaperBroker (global)
nodes.rationale: COMMISSION_PCT/COMMISSION_PER_ORDER charged on every fill and stored in trade_orders.commission; global to all versions so churn is priced fairly in the A/B; remains an adapter detail, seam intact.

nodes.label: P12: data-freshness gate (MAX_BAR_STALENESS_DAYS)
nodes.rationale: Excludes a symbol from scoring/execution when its latest bar is too many sessions stale — low euro impact in paper, important for a real broker.

nodes.label: Strategy v4 (= v3 + cross-sectional momentum)
nodes.rationale: Activates P11 phase 1 only (momentum); phase 2 (macro multiplier) deferred to v5 to keep one variable per experiment.

nodes.label: PriceMomentum indicator (126-bar return, skip 21)
nodes.rationale: 12-1-style momentum with a 6-month lookback (loaded history was too short for 252+21); params live in the base config so all versions compute/persist it in observation mode while only v4+ weight it; with rank_normalize it becomes relative momentum across the day's universe.

nodes.label: Stale high_water_mark on re-entry bug (HIGH)
nodes.rationale: high_water_mark was never cleared on close/re-buy, so a re-entered position inherited the prior trip's peak and could stop out on the first tick, creating a buy-sell loop every cooldown. Fixed in PaperBroker for all versions; part of v1's live churn was this bug, not strategy.

nodes.label: Strategy v5 (= v4 + macro regime multiplier)
nodes.rationale: scoring.regime_multiplier (floor 0.75 / ceil 1.05) linearly scales every composite by the 0-100 macro regime score, damping exposure up to -25% under stress while barely touching risk-on.
nodes.norm_label: strategy v5 (= v4 + macro regime multiplier)

nodes.label: Strategy v6 (= v5 + fundamental weights)
nodes.rationale: Activates quality 0.15 / revenue_accel 0.10 / earnings_accel 0.10 — the signals that had been in observation mode; missing fundamentals renormalize, never impute. Live experiment later invalidated by a Finnhub 429 data freeze.

nodes.label: Backtester (backend/backtest/)
nodes.rationale: Replays the LIVE pipeline (same engine, sizing, stop math, cost knobs) over stored bars day by day, with anti-look-ahead rules (signals on d-1 data, fills at d's open, fundamentals lagged 45 days, VIX/regime recomputed per day). Built because 1 day of live evidence per calendar day was the project's learning bottleneck; became the mandatory gate for shipping any strategy change.

nodes.label: Thesis-breaker: v1 wins the long backtest
nodes.rationale: Over 2024-09 to 2026-06 (~440 sessions) v1 returned +52.2% (Sharpe 1.01, only version beating SPY) while the v2-v6 'improvements' all underperformed — the diagnosis had overfit ~10 unrepresentative bearish live sessions; all defensive fixes reduced participation in a bull trend. Burden of proof inverted onto the defensive versions; no arm killed on a single backtest.
nodes.norm_label: thesis-breaker: v1 wins the long backtest

nodes.label: Market entry filter (benchmark below long MA blocks BUYs)
nodes.rationale: Universe-wide absolute gate in the base config: when SPY closes below its 200d MA, every BUY downgrades to HOLD (exits never blocked), so a fresh portfolio waits in cash for an uptrend — the piece rank-normalized versions could not provide since they always find a relative best. 200d chosen over 100d as the standard, most out-of-sample-robust line; accepted return cost in the bull window because its value appears in sustained bear markets absent from the calibration window. Fail-open on missing data.
nodes.norm_label: market entry filter (benchmark below long ma blocks buys)

nodes.label: Strategy v7 (= v3 + wider stops ATRx3.5, floor 7%)
nodes.rationale: Backtest candidate c4: halves stop-outs and doubles win% in chop at similar return; selected because it improved or matched v3 in BOTH the sideways and the long multi-regime window.
nodes.norm_label: strategy v7 (= v3 + wider stops atrx3.5, floor 7%)

nodes.label: Strategy v8 (regime_switch ensemble v1-trend / v3-chop)
nodes.rationale: Scores the universe with v1's config when SPY is at/above its 100d MA and v3's below, inside DefaultAnalysisEngine (fail-open to the chop leg, nesting forbidden); trading knobs are NOT switched — v3's execution discipline in every regime, because backtests showed most of v1's live loss was execution, not signal.

nodes.label: Finding: no version dominates both regimes
nodes.rationale: v1 (absolute threshold, momentum) won the 2024-25 trend backtest but was worst live in the 2026 sideways window (-11.6%); v3 (relative rank) the reverse. The backtester reproduced the live ranking over the same window, proving regime dependence rather than backtester failure — the most solid conclusion of the whole live A/B and the rationale for the regime-switch ensemble.
nodes.norm_label: finding: no version dominates both regimes

nodes.label: v9 trading_from_leg — REJECTED (negative result)
nodes.rationale: Letting the active leg supply entry discipline (pyramiding etc.) failed because the MA100 detector cannot distinguish advance from drift: in the 2026 lateral SPY never closed below MA100 so v9 ran the aggressive leg all period (identical to v1, -7.4%). Mechanism kept in code, off by default; validated that per-leg pyramiding captures trend (+18.7%).

nodes.label: Strategy v10 (v9 mechanism + 21-session momentum confirmation)
nodes.rationale: Aggressive leg requires SPY above MA100 AND positive 21-session return; 21-session momentum distinguishes advance from drift where MA100 and mom63 failed. First project strategy to beat SPY in the long window (+44.8% vs +32.1%); validated on a third never-used OOS window (Sharpe 1.94) under the new rule: 2 calibration windows + 1 OOS.

nodes.label: s1 equal-risk sizing (trading.vol_target_pct) — DISCARDED
nodes.rationale: Risk a fixed % of value per position using ATR-multiple stop distance as the risk unit (never leverage, MAX_POSITION_PCT stays the ceiling). Discarded: shrinking volatile names shrinks the rebounds mean-reversion exploits, losing the lateral window; mechanism kept in code off by default for momentum-based futures.

nodes.label: m3 low-frequency micro (max_trades_per_day + min_hold_minutes)
nodes.rationale: m1's forward-test showed ~zero gross edge eaten by ~26 round-trips/day of friction, so m3 attacks friction not signal: per-session BUY budget, min-hold window for signal exits (protective stops and EOD flatten exempt), min_score_to_act 75. Decision rule: if no micro version beats cash net of costs in 4 weeks, the micro track shuts down.

nodes.label: Cost attribution endpoint (GET /api/portfolios/{id}/costs)
nodes.rationale: Splits commissions vs estimated slippage vs realized flow so 'no edge' is distinguishable from 'edge eaten by costs' without manual analysis.

nodes.label: Phantom-sell race (run_micro x micro_eod_flatten)
nodes.rationale: Duplicate sells from concurrent micro jobs minted cash; fixed with a shared asyncio lock, run_micro standing down in the flatten window, and a row-locked (FOR UPDATE) sell-coverage check in PaperBroker; contaminated fills voided and micro NAV rebuilt from ledgers.

nodes.label: strategy_version identifier (semver+config_hash)
nodes.rationale: config_hash over the canonicalised resolved config is the safety net: editing a weight without bumping semver still records a distinct version, so two different configs can never silently share a label. Stamped at the job write boundary so the scorer stays version-agnostic.

nodes.label: Significance tests (bootstrap, Jobson-Korkie/Memmel, two-proportion z)
nodes.rationale: Bootstrap beats t-test normality assumptions on fat-tailed small-n returns; Jobson-Korkie with Memmel correction is the standard Sharpe-difference test. Reporting 'no significant difference' is a first-class answer that prevents overfitting to noise.

nodes.label: Regime confound in sequential A/B
nodes.rationale: Sequential experiments live in different market regimes, so 'v2 beat v1' may mean 'v2 ran during a bull market' — the single biggest threat to validity. Mitigated by regime tagging, within-regime comparison, alpha-first metrics, and (later realized) parallel shadow portfolios.

nodes.label: Parallel shadow experiments (per-portfolio strategy_label)
nodes.rationale: Multiple virtual portfolios scored by different versions on identical data eliminate the regime confound; realized ahead of schedule via portfolios.strategy_label + config overlays, with the daily engine trading every portfolio under its own version on the same universe/day.

nodes.label: summarize_performance envelope (returns/risk/trades)
nodes.rationale: Single entry point bundling all headline metrics in the exact shape reporting-structure and the Experiment Tracker consume — pure functions, DataFrame in, typed result out, nan on degenerate input.

nodes.label: build_round_trips (FIFO lot matcher)
nodes.rationale: FIFO, long-only round-trip construction from trade_orders; open positions produce no trip so trade-level metrics are realized-only by design, with unrealized captured by NAV metrics — avoiding double-counting.

nodes.label: PerformanceThresholds (what good looks like)
nodes.rationale: Sharpe>=1, maxDD shallower than -20%, PF>=1.5, alpha>0 over >=30 trips and >=3 months; lives in code (evaluation) not strategy.yaml (behavior). Win rate is never read alone — always paired with profit factor.

nodes.label: Health vs strategy-quality diagnostic split
nodes.rationale: A broken pipeline and a losing strategy look different in the data: flat NAV + green health + RISK_OFF is correct behavior; flat NAV + failed job is a break. If any health indicator is red, performance numbers are suspect and the dashboard must say so via a banner, never a silently stale chart.

nodes.label: Nine dashboard summary cards spec
nodes.rationale: Cards 1-6 performance (P&L palette), cards 7-9 context/health (status palette), never interleaved — the load-bearing UX rule that money and health never share a color language.

nodes.label: summary.json export schema (A/B join surface)
nodes.rationale: strategy_version + period + returns/risk/activity keys form the contract the Experiment Tracker comparator joins on; risk keys mirror Financial Analyst metric names exactly so no remapping is needed.

nodes.label: Blocker: benchmark_value never written
nodes.rationale: snapshot_nav inserts only cash/equity/total, so alpha/beta/benchmark are permanently nan and the SPY overlay never renders — the single highest-impact analytics gap; fix is writing the SPY close into benchmark_value.

nodes.label: Blocker: nan/inf breaks /portfolio/performance JSON
nodes.rationale: summarize_performance emits real nan (alpha/beta with no benchmark) and inf (profit_factor with no losses); the default JSON response either raises (allow_nan=False -> 500) or emits tokens JSON.parse rejects — so the endpoint fails in the normal post-day-1 state. Fix: sanitize non-finite floats to null at the API boundary.

nodes.label: CR2: mock_real broker cash bypasses the adapter
nodes.rationale: PortfolioManager recomputed cash from the DB ledger while total came from the broker, so MockRealBroker's numbers never reconciled and RiskManager sized against wrong figures — a violation of the swap guarantee; cash must come from the broker too.
nodes.norm_label: cr2: mock_real broker cash bypasses the adapter

nodes.label: MUST FIX (fixed): Twelve Data API key leaked via exceptions
nodes.rationale: raise_for_status outside try/except let httpx errors carrying apikey=<SECRET> in the URL propagate into logs, job_runs.error, and the unauthenticated /api/system/status response; fixed with a redaction helper and re-raise as ProviderError from None.
nodes.norm_label: must fix (fixed): twelve data api key leaked via exceptions

nodes.label: Signal priority matrix (31 signals, 3 tiers)
nodes.rationale: Ranked by evidence strength, free availability, complexity, 1-4 week horizon alignment, and uniqueness; Tier 1 is 100% yfinance/FRED with no NLP or scraping so it ships first.

nodes.label: Composite scoring pipeline (7 steps to final_score)
nodes.rationale: Regime classify -> technical + fundamental sub-scores -> bounded sentiment overlay + event tags -> macro multiplier x rotation tilt x calendar factor; every weight is a config/strategy.yaml stub to be calibrated by the Experiment Tracker, never hardcoded.
nodes.norm_label: composite scoring pipeline (7 steps to final_score)

nodes.label: Macro regime filter (RISK_ON/CAUTION/RISK_OFF multiplier)
nodes.rationale: Built from curve + VIX + VIX term + credit + breadth + SPY trend votes with 2-day hysteresis; multiplies the composite (1.1/0.6/0.3, bounded [0.3,1.2]) and sets profile bias, with a VIX>40 panic floor so the system never sells the capitulation.

nodes.label: Cross-sectional rank normalization (anti-domination)
nodes.rationale: Percentile-rank each raw signal across the universe before weighting so one outlier metric cannot blow out the composite; bounded overlays and a bounded multiplier ensure overlays nudge, never override.

nodes.label: Two regime layers compose, never both multiply
nodes.rationale: The global macro regime is dominant (multiplier + profile bias); the per-symbol classifier only selects which technical weight-profile computes the sub-score — preventing double-counting of the regime read.
nodes.norm_label: two regime layers compose, never both multiply

nodes.label: Missing-data renormalization (never impute zero)
nodes.rationale: Unavailable signals are dropped and remaining weights renormalized so a missing fundamental never silently penalizes well-covered names; absence of good news is not bad news; data_completeness persisted per symbol/date for diagnostics.

nodes.label: PEAD single ownership (fundamental computes SUE, event tag consumes)
nodes.rationale: Earnings surprise appeared in two research streams; one computation, one stored value, two readers avoids double-counting the most-replicated event anomaly in the composite.
nodes.norm_label: pead single ownership (fundamental computes sue, event tag consumes)

nodes.label: 50-symbol watchlist (runtime-seeded)
nodes.rationale: 5 benchmark ETFs + 11 sector SPDRs + 3 factor ETFs + 31 stocks covering all 11 GICS sectors; annotated coverage gaps (BRK-B, NEM, PLD) deliberately exercise the missing-data renormalization path; populated at runtime, never hardcoded.

nodes.label: Blended cross-sectional momentum (12-1, 52w-high, dual RS)
nodes.rationale: Jegadeesh & Titman momentum plus George & Hwang 52-week-high proximity; the 1-month skip removes short-term reversal contamination. The strongest documented technical edge and the highest-weight recommended input.

nodes.label: Per-symbol regime classifier (efficiency ratio + ADX)
nodes.rationale: The same indicator means opposite things in different regimes; a per-symbol trending-vs-choppy classifier switching momentum vs reversion weight profiles is the highest-leverage technical design decision.

nodes.label: Quality composite (FCF yield + ROE trend + margin trend)
nodes.rationale: Fully yfinance-computable quality premium (Novy-Marx / Asness QMJ); pairs best as a filter on momentum — quality momentum outperforms momentum alone and reduces crashes.
nodes.norm_label: quality composite (fcf yield + roe trend + margin trend)

nodes.label: SUE / standardized earnings surprise
nodes.rationale: Bernard & Thomas underreaction: drift persists ~60 days in the surprise direction; data quality of free consensus estimates (thin in yfinance) is the binding constraint, resolved by budgeting Finnhub free tier.

nodes.label: PEAD decaying event tag
nodes.rationale: On a confirmed beat/miss attach a decaying bonus (~30-45 trading days) gated by the day-1 reaction sign; the most evidence-backed signal of the whole news stream because the drift is multi-day, exactly what a daily batch can harvest.

nodes.label: Insider Form 4 open-market buying (cluster + role-weighted)
nodes.rationale: Strongest free smart-money alpha (Lakonishok & Lee; Cohen/Malloy/Pomorski): buying is informative, selling is noise; cluster buying (>=3 insiders in 30 days) is the strongest variant. OpenInsider for prototype, SEC EDGAR as the hardened provider.

nodes.label: 8-K material-event detection (item codes + keyword polarity)
nodes.rationale: 8-Ks are the earliest structured free authoritative signal of corporate events; item-code priors plus lightweight keyword polarity (no on-Pi NLP) give multi-day tradeable drift on items like restatements.

nodes.label: Correction: alternative.me is crypto-only
nodes.rationale: The CLAUDE.md data-source table wrongly listed alternative.me as an equity Fear & Greed gauge; the equity F&G concept is rebuilt from owned components (VIX + put/call + breadth + momentum) instead of scraping CNN's fragile undocumented endpoint.

nodes.label: RISK_ON/CAUTION/RISK_OFF regime classifier (stream 03)
nodes.rationale: Vote-based classification over curve, cycle phase, VIX level/term structure, credit (HYG/IEF), breadth (RSP/SPY), SPY vs 200d MA; acts as a post-multiplier on every bottom-up score, never a separate composite signal; hysteresis prevents one-day whipsaw.

nodes.label: Breadth ETF proxy (RSP/SPY, IWM/SPY)
nodes.rationale: Downloading ~503 S&P components daily is slow, fragile, and RAM-heavy on a 4GB Pi; the equal-weight/cap-weight ratio captures most A/D-divergence information for the cost of two daily bars.

nodes.label: Sector rotation model (cycle phase -> sector tilt)
nodes.rationale: Directionally real but noisy as a timer; treated as a bounded +/-15% tilt confirmed by relative strength, never a hard switch — most useful at cycle extremes.
nodes.norm_label: sector rotation model (cycle phase -> sector tilt)

nodes.label: VWAP trend/reversion strategy (micro spine)
nodes.rationale: Session-anchored VWAP is a real institutional coordination point; trend leg rides confirmed accumulation, reversion leg fades over-extension on low RVOL; 45-55% hit-rate at R:R >= 1.3 before costs.

nodes.label: Opening-Range Breakout (ORB)
nodes.rationale: The first 15-30 min concentrates overnight price discovery; a confirmed break marks the auction winner. Low win-rate (35-45%) but high R:R — the opposite profile of reversion, which is exactly why m1 vs m2 contrasts them.

nodes.label: Relative-volume (RVOL) gate
nodes.rationale: Time-of-day-normalized participation proxy; a gate, not a weight — high volume confirms direction but doesn't provide it, so it multiplies/thresholds entries rather than joining the weighted composite (analogous to the daily market_filter layering).

nodes.label: End-of-day (last-30-min) momentum (Heston et al. 2010)
nodes.rationale: Last-half-hour return is predicted by the first-half-hour return — the highest-evidence intraday signal and the most cost-robust per unit time because the exit is a clock, not a price.

nodes.label: Cost-aware micro action gate (min_edge_mult)
nodes.rationale: Only take a setup whose projected ATR target clears a multiple of the round-trip cost — the micro analogue of min_score_to_act, but cost-aware, because at micro ticket size costs, not alpha, are the first-order term.

nodes.label: Micro universe (12-20 liquid high-ATR subset + morning RVOL ranker)
nodes.rationale: Day-trading edge is concentrated in names in play; breadth hurts here (opposite of the multi-week sleeve), intraday polling cost is linear in universe size, and half the daily watchlist has no intraday amplitude. Stays runtime data, never hardcoded.
nodes.norm_label: micro universe (12-20 liquid high-atr subset + morning rvol ranker)

nodes.label: m1/m2 proposal: entry-pattern contrast (EOD+VWAP vs ORB)
nodes.rationale: m1 = most cost-robust, lowest-frequency patterns (EOD momentum + VWAP trend); m2 swaps only the entry legs to ORB — isolating the low-win-rate/high-R:R vs high-win-rate/low-R:R meta-question with everything else held constant.
nodes.norm_label: m1/m2 proposal: entry-pattern contrast (eod+vwap vs orb)

nodes.label: Intraday bars provider chain (yfinance -> Alpaca IEX -> Twelve Data)
nodes.rationale: Single IntradayBarsProvider Protocol with each hop raising RateLimitError to trigger the next; every stage degrades to keep-last-good + mark incompleteness, never blocks. Alpaca IEX added as the robust fallback (free WS, multi-year history, doubles as Phase-2 broker groundwork; IEX = ~2-3% of tape, flagged); Twelve Data bounded to 800 credits/day is a stopgap, not steady-state.
nodes.norm_label: intraday bars provider chain (yfinance -> alpaca iex -> twelve data)

nodes.label: Finding: Finnhub free does NOT serve candles (403)
nodes.rationale: The brief assumed the existing FINNHUB_API_KEY unlocked intraday bars; verified June 2026 that /stock/candle moved to premium tiers, returning 403 on free keys — the single fact that reordered the whole provider chain. Finnhub stays for news/quotes/financials only.
nodes.norm_label: finding: finnhub free does not serve candles (403)

nodes.label: intraday_bars hypertable (PK symbol, ts, interval)
nodes.rationale: market_bars is daily-only by construction (PK has no interval); a separate hypertable with compression + short retention keeps 5m data from outgrowing the Pi, with a source column recording the IEX-partial-volume caveat.

nodes.label: Micro validation: forward-test, not short backtest
nodes.rationale: No free multi-regime intraday history exists (yfinance ~60 days of 5m = one regime); calibrating on it is exactly the overfitting that produced v2-v6 losing to v1. Discipline: persist own 5m bars from day one, validate via a dedicated micro paper portfolio forward-test, treat 60-day backtests as plumbing checks only.
nodes.norm_label: micro validation: forward-test, not short backtest

nodes.label: Micro break-even math (spread+slippage+commission)
nodes.rationale: Spread+slippage set a ~0.05-0.15% per-trade floor even at zero commission; a per-order fee on a 100 EUR ticket demands a 2.05% intraday move to break even, making small tickets economically dead — ticket size is the lever, and percentage commissions are preferred for small portfolios.

nodes.label: Turnover multiplies cost drag (the enemy)
nodes.rationale: Cost is paid per round trip; 5 trades/day at a 0.05% break-even burns ~63%/yr before any edge — so max_trades_per_day is the primary cost-control lever, not a nicety. There is no free microtrading.

nodes.label: Seven intraday risk rails (loss limit, trade cap, time-stop...)
nodes.rationale: Deterministic, config-driven gates over existing state: daily loss limit, max trades/day, max concurrent positions, per-trade risk %, time-stop, hard trailing stop, forced EOD flatten — mapped onto the protective_sell interval-job pattern with no new broker method.
nodes.norm_label: seven intraday risk rails (loss limit, trade cap, time-stop...)

nodes.label: Forced end-of-day flatten (never hold overnight)
nodes.rationale: Overnight gap risk defeats the same-day premise; non-negotiable, and it must read the actual (possibly half-day) session close from the market calendar — flattening 10 min before 4 PM on a 1 PM half-day strands positions.

nodes.label: Pattern Day Trader rule ($25k) and settlement caveats
nodes.rationale: A 500 EUR account cannot legally day-trade on a US margin broker (~50x below the PDT floor) and T+1 settlement throttles cash-account round trips — so the 500 EUR micro portfolio is illustrative only; a deployable read needs >= ~25-30k.
nodes.norm_label: pattern day trader rule ($25k) and settlement caveats

nodes.label: Micro-specific metrics (expectancy, cost drag, trades/day, hold time, intraday DD)
nodes.rationale: NAV-level metrics are too coarse for a high-turnover sleeve; per-trade expectancy net of costs and cost-drag (% of gross eaten by costs) make a losing scalper visible per-trade where Sharpe would take months; max intraday drawdown requires sub-daily NAV snapshots.
nodes.norm_label: micro-specific metrics (expectancy, cost drag, trades/day, hold time, intraday dd)

nodes.label: m1/m2 proposal: turnover contrast (max_trades_per_day 3 vs 6)
nodes.rationale: This stream's one-variable m1/m2 pair tests whether more turnover earns net profit or just cost drag — prior: less turnover wins, mirroring the backtest finding that the simpler control beat the improvements. Requires the realistic spread/slippage cost model switched on first or every micro result is fiction.
